feedback.summary: You produced a strong, balanced ethics analysis with a clear Not to Ship recommendation supported by the EA Code and relevant external cases. Your introduction, discussion and recommendation sections show excellent stakeholder awareness and structure. To reach Excellent across all criteria, deepen stakeholder-specific guidance, add quantitative evidence, and include visual elements with consistent referencing.

criteria.C1: You excelled here. In INTRODUCTION you identified several issues – public safety/harm, professional integrity, reputation and business survival – and linked them to competitive product cycles. You explicitly mapped stakeholders from Rachel and her company to the chip contractor and end-users.
criteria.C2: Strong depth in DISCUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship where you set out for-arguments like revenue and job security and against-arguments on harm. For Excellent, add distinct decision recommendations for each stakeholder in The Most Ethical Path, not just Rachel.
criteria.C3: Excellent structure – your argument flows from ABSTRACT through INTRODUCTION to The Most Ethical Path and CONCLUSION where you argue "severity of potential harm to end-users cannot be understated" to support "decision to Not Ship is certainly the most ethical path", with systematic EA Code linkage.
criteria.C4: Good research base with 4 references including Engineers Australia Code Of Ethics, BBC/NHS case, and VW emissions. You use qualitative harm evidence well in The Most Ethical Path. For Excellent, add quantitative evidence – e.g., failure percentages, cost of recall, HSSIB impact numbers.
criteria.C5: Your report is fluent with clear sections functioning well, including ABSTRACT stating "This report examines an ethical dilemma for a quality assurance engineer". To reach Very good/Excellent, include visual elements such as a stakeholder map or risk table and ensure References are consistently formatted with full links.
